sections.title: Form and cultivation
sections.text: A cultivated perennial, usually about 30–40 cm tall, forming clumps of hollow, cylindrical leaves. Its base can be swollen, but it does not develop the large bulb of the common onion. Small greenish-white flowers grow in umbels. Kew gives China as its cultivated origin; it is now widely grown.

sections.title: Food and comparison
sections.text: The leaves are eaten. Welsh onion belongs to the same genus as garlic and onion, but its tubular leaves and lack of a true bulb distinguish it from the bulb-forming onion.
